title: Demo rubric (original, not XQ)
note: Written for this repo so tests and the notebook run offline. It is not an XQ document and has not been validated for classroom use.

skills.name: Checks reasonableness
skills.description: Tests whether a numerical result makes sense before accepting it.

levels.1: Accepts a result without comparing it to anything.
levels.2: Compares a result to an estimate when prompted.
levels.3: Compares a result to an estimate or known bound without prompting and states whether it fits.
levels.4: Uses a second method or bound to confirm a result and explains any mismatch.

skills.name: States angle units
skills.description: Keeps track of whether angles are in degrees or radians.

levels.1: Writes angle values with no unit.
levels.2: Labels some angle values with a unit.
levels.3: Labels angle values consistently and matches the calculator mode to the unit.
levels.4: Converts between degrees and radians when a problem mixes them and shows the conversion.

skills.name: Draws a labeled diagram
skills.description: Turns a written situation into a diagram with the known and unknown parts marked.

levels.1: Draws a shape that does not match the situation.
levels.2: Draws a matching shape with some parts labeled.
levels.3: Draws a matching shape with all given lengths and angles labeled and the unknown marked.
levels.4: Draws a labeled diagram and uses it to choose which relationship to apply.

skills.name: Sets up a trig ratio
skills.description: Chooses sine, cosine, or tangent from the sides a right triangle gives.

levels.1: Writes a ratio that does not use the given sides.
levels.2: Writes a correct ratio with sides named but the wrong side in the numerator or denominator.
levels.3: Writes the correct ratio for the given sides and solves for the unknown.
levels.4: Writes the correct ratio and explains why the other two ratios do not fit the given sides.

skills.name: Interprets a result in context
skills.description: Says what a calculated number means for the situation it came from.

levels.1: Gives a number with no statement of what it means.
levels.2: Gives a number with a unit.
levels.3: States what the number means in the situation, with a unit.
levels.4: States what the number means and names a limit of the model that produced it.

skills.name: Explains reasoning in writing
skills.description: Writes the steps and the reason for each step so a reader can follow them.

levels.1: Writes an answer with no steps.
levels.3: Writes steps with a reason for each main step.
levels.4: Writes steps and reasons that a classmate could follow to solve a similar problem.

skills.name: Revises after feedback
skills.description: Changes work in response to a check or comment and says what changed.

levels.2: Changes the answer without showing what changed.
levels.3: Corrects the step that caused the error and marks the change.
levels.4: Corrects the step, marks the change, and states how to avoid the error next time.

skills.name: Uses precise vocabulary
skills.description: Uses terms such as opposite, adjacent, hypotenuse, and angle of elevation correctly.

levels.1: Uses no mathematical terms or uses them incorrectly.
levels.3: Uses the needed terms correctly throughout.
levels.4: Uses terms correctly and defines one for a reader who might not know it.
